analysis.title: BP Plc (BP.L): 3Q26 First Take: Earnings beat drive strong cash flow generation and deleveraging
key_insights: BP 3Q26 underlying RC operating profit was US$13,443mn, c.10% above company-compiled consensus of US$12,230mn. Underlying RC net income was US$8,458mn, c.15% above consensus of US$7,330mn.

Customers & products RC operating profit was US$6,948mn, c.10% above consensus of US$6,300mn. Refining had significantly higher realized margins, stronger commercial optimization and lower turnaround activity. Oil trading was slightly higher QoQ.

Oil Production & Operations RC operating profit was US$3,534mn, c.5% above consensus of US$3,350mn. Gas & low carbon energy was US$3,183mn, c.11% above the US$2,860mn consensus, on higher realizations and significantly stronger gas marketing & trading.

Operating cash flow before working capital movements was US$14.3bn versus VA consensus of $12.9bn. Capex was US$3.0bn, implying free cash flow of c.US$11.3bn before working capital. A US$0.5bn working capital release was also reported.
Net debt-to-equity fell to 34% from 47% in 2Q26, a deleveraging step. The 3Q26 DPS of 8.66 cents was flat QoQ and in line with GS expectations.

4Q26 upstream production guidance is 2,090-2,230 kboe/d versus 2,215 kboe/d in 3Q26. Drivers are continued Middle East disruption, bpx activity phasing, seasonal gas demand and an estimated c.20 kboe/d hit from potential Gulf of America weather, partly offset by recovery from outages.

BP expects a significantly lower Customers result QoQ in 4Q26 on seasonal volumes, a lower midstream contribution and lower Castrol earnings. Products throughput is guided to 1,160-1,210 kb/d versus 1,396 kb/d in 3Q26 on the Gelsenkirchen divestment and higher planned maintenance. Cash taxes paid are expected to be around $0.8bn higher QoQ.

FY2026 reported upstream production guidance narrowed to 2,210-2,250 kboe/d from 2,180-2,270 kboe/d. Products throughput guidance narrowed to 1,390-1,400 kb/d from 1,360-1,410 kb/d. The underlying tax rate was lowered to 31-34% from 35-40%.

Capex guidance is unchanged at $13.5-14.0bn, DD&A at $17.0-17.5bn and other businesses & corporate charges at around $1bn. Divestment and other proceeds are now expected at around $8bn versus $8-9bn at 2Q26, including approximately $6bn from the Castrol transaction, expected to complete imminently.
GS rates BP Buy with 12-month price targets of 720p and US$57.0 (ADR), based on 5.0x EV/DACF on 2028E cash flow. Upside is 15.3% for BP.L at 624.3p and 13.2% for the ADR at $50.35.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy after the 3Q26 beat on operating profit and cash flow, with a 12-month ADR target of $57.00 and 720p for BP.L based on 5.0x EV/DACF on 2028E cash flow.

earnings_insights: BP 3Q26 underlying RC operating profit reported 10/30 at US$13,443mn vs company-compiled consensus est US$12,230mn and GS est US$12,250mn.

BP 3Q26 underlying RC net income (RC adjusted net income) reported at US$8,458mn vs company-compiled consensus est US$7,330mn and GS est US$7,492mn. RC reported net income was US$4,696mn, after post-tax exceptionals of US$3,762mn.
BP 3Q26 pro forma clean EPS reported at $0.55 vs GS est $0.49, versus $0.37 in 2Q26 and $0.14 in 3Q25.
BP 3Q26 operating cash flow reported at US$14,298mn vs GS est US$12,500mn. Capex reported at US$3,036mn vs GS est US$3,000mn.
BP 3Q26 effective tax rate was 28% vs GS est 30% and company-compiled consensus est 31%. Tax charge was US$3,524mn vs consensus est US$3,430mn.
BP 3Q26 total production reported at 2,220 kboe/d vs GS est 2,215 kboe/d, down 6% y/y.
GS EPS estimates: FY26E $1.40, FY27E $0.92, FY28E $0.74. 4Q26E EPS is $0.33. FY2025 EPS was $0.48.
risk_factors: Lower than expected oil and gas prices or exploration success.
Negative surprises to growth or capex.
Seasonal weather events in the Gulf of America, estimated at c.20 kboe/d of 4Q26 production impact.
Significantly lower Customers & products result in 4Q26 on seasonal volumes, lower midstream contribution and lower Castrol earnings.
geopolitical: Continued disruption in the Middle East is cited by BP as a drag on 4Q26 upstream production.
